## 3. Is the wire on the agent path?

O1 rules that agent evals are co-located with the database: a read is a pointer
into an immutable value, a write is a function call. Check whether that is true
yet.

```
rg -n 'open-session!|writer-socket-path' src/seon/db/host.clj | head -4
```

```
42:  [{::keys [writer-socket-path database-name backend database-path
48:     (cond-> {::writer-socket-path writer-socket-path
183:  [{::keys [writer-socket-path database-name interest-state] :as writer}]
184:  (let [session (uds/open-session! writer-socket-path)
```

**VERDICT: the wire is still on the agent path.** `writer-session` opens a
UDS session to a separate `writer` process, so every agent read and write
crosses a socket. O1 co-location is the target, not the state.

## 5. Where work is bounded, and where it is not

Backpressure is one idea with four different expressions. This is the table that
decides whether the scheduling design is needed.

| submission point | bound | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| SCI eval | YES — semaphore | `rg -c Semaphore src/seon/sci/eval.clj` → 4 |
| transactions (Datahike side) | ALWAYS bounded | `create-writer :self` builds `transaction-queue` + `commit-queue`; defaults `DEFAULT_QUEUE_SIZE` / `DEFAULT_COMMIT_WAIT_TIME 0` |
| transactions (Seon supplies values?) | YES | committed: 21 hits · working tree: 21 hits |
| run admission | NO — unbounded spawn | `rg -c "start-virtual-thread!" src/seon/agent/driver.clj` → 4 call sites, none behind a permit |
| agent capability calls | NO | `rg -c Semaphore src/seon/db/host.clj src/seon/ai/http.clj` → 0 |

## 6. The corpus round trip

Three independent things must hold for an agent's `defn` to survive: it is
written as facts, it is installed at boot, and form 2 of a reply can see form 1.

| property | state | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| authored fn written as facts | **MISSING** | `rg -c tee-tx-data src/` → 0 |
| corpus installed at boot | **MISSING** | `rg -c "install-nursery!|rebuild!" src/` → 0 |
| form 1 visible to form 2 | BUILT | driver passes a base ctx → 1 hits |
| `:seon.fn/execution-tier` kind stamp | gone (R-19a satisfied) | `rg -c` → 0 |

## 8. Can the machine prove anything?

The JVM gate needs the compiled program artifact, so it reports zero tests until
a `bin/seon up` / `bin/seon down` freeze rebuilds it. A full `bin/test-writer`
run tees its own retained evidence to `tmp/plan-evidence/test-writer-latest.log`;
dated copies in the same directory are archives.

Last retained run — `tmp/plan-evidence/test-writer-latest.log` (2026-07-26):

```
<no summary line>
<no result line>
```

**INCOMPLETE — do not read this as green.** The log has no
`N failures, N errors.` line, so the run did not finish (still writing,
killed, or crashed before the summary). Absence of `FAIL in` lines in an
unfinished log proves nothing.

## 10. Dangling attribute references

An attribute read or written with no `schema/register!` anywhere. Each is a real
defect: the read returns nil and any sort over it is meaningless.

```
:seon\.ai\.attempt/*  distinct used: 2   registered: 0
:seon\.agent\.turn/*  distinct used: 15   registered: 0
```
